correctness.rationale: For any bounded family in a separable Banach space, countable ball covers plus countable completeness force an ultrafilter-large ball at every radius; the selected centers are Cauchy, proving surjectivity of the diagonal embedding. The octahedrality of \(\ell_1\) is witnessed by a coordinate where finitely many vectors are small. Non-rigid octahedrality is certified by \(x=(2^{-n})_{n\ge1}\) and \(-x\): equality in both \(\ell_1\) triangle inequalities would force a unit witness to be simultaneously coordinatewise nonnegative and nonpositive. All quantifiers and boundary assumptions were checked.

originality.rationale: The final claim is not the diagonal-collapse theorem itself. It identifies an assumption boundary of the 2026 rigidification result by combining the countably complete collapse with an explicit octahedral-but-not-rigid witness in \(\ell_1\). Searches for the exact implication, aliases, and broader ultrapower formulations found the recent positive theorem and the older collapse theorem but no source stating this sharpness consequence. value.rationale: The finding isolates a mathematically natural boundary of a new ultrapower rigidification theorem. It shows that countable incompleteness is not merely a proof convenience: in the opposite ultrafilter regime the ultrapower of the canonical octahedral example \(\ell_1\) can collapse and fail even the weakest exact rigidification. This is a motivated structural counterexample rather than an arbitrary special case.
